discussion_comments.comment_body: We can’t do that, which is why I had to revert the change in https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6991/changes/bf678ff1f4568cae16f24035a9e8d9c4fab64d38.
I still don't understand, why not to use 'utf8' encoding in http header? Node buffer use alias 'utf8' for utf-8 encoding. What we achieved by doing this separation?

> I still don't understand, why not to use 'utf8' encoding in http header? Node buffer use alias 'utf8' for utf-8 encoding.

This encoding name is what ends up in HTTP header, `utf8` is not a [valid value](https://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets/character-sets.xhtml) there and makes the tests [fail](https://github.com/expressjs/express/actions/runs/21080370093) ([RFC 9110](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#rfc.section.8.3.2)).

> `utf8` is not a [valid value](https://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets/character-sets.xhtml)

I know this also modern browsers understand utf8. I did some research, only node use utf8 in buffers, others like Django use utf-8.
`/^[\w!#$&+.^`|~-]+\*?$/` would be the exact same as the productions in [rfc5988](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5988#section-5) (see the link-extension production)

This (and line 106) only allow quoted-string values. Token and extended notation values should also be allowed. hreflang, for example, only allows tokens. title\* only allows extended notation values. See [rfc5988](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5988#section-5).

This will fail for non-normalized values, like `FE80::1` or even `fe80:0:0:0:0:0:0:1`; it also doesn't detect the IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses Node.js 0.12+ provided on dual stacks, which is `::ffff:127.0.0.1`

I ran into a similar issue with 2.5.9 and the `*/*` "fix". The problem is that most browsers send `*/*` at the end of the accepts header as a catch all. What really begins to matter is the order of the mime types in the accept header. Personally I think it is wrong to handle the _/_ case in the framework. It is much easier for a user to decide what their default _catch all_ case should be rather than all accepts methods returning true when `*/*` is present.

I view the `req.accepts(<some type here>)` code as a way to see if that particular mime type is explicitly accepted and not implicitly. Personally, I would be in favor of reverting this change. Handling the `*/*` case is better done at the app level.
